Pre-Expedition Intelligence

Uganda Travel & Planning FAQ

How far in advance must I secure my Uganda gorilla tracking permit?

We strongly advise reserving your mountain gorilla permits at least 4 to 8 months in advance, particularly for travel during peak dry periods (June to September and December to February). The Uganda Wildlife Authority limits permits strictly to 8 visitors per habituated gorilla family per day to preserve their health and habitat.

What is the official minimum age for tracking gorillas in Uganda?

The legal minimum age established by the Uganda Wildlife Authority is 15 years old on the date of tracking. A valid passport copy is submitted to UWA headquarters during the permit verification and issuance process.

Are domestic bush flights available between parks?

Yes. For travelers wishing to reduce overland driving times, daily scheduled light aircraft flights operate from Entebbe International Airport directly to airstrips in Kihihi and Kisoro (for Bwindi), Kasese and Mweya (for Queen Elizabeth), Pakuba and Bugungu (for Murchison Falls), and Apoka (for Kidepo Valley).

What health and vaccination documentation is required to enter Uganda?

A valid Yellow Fever vaccination certificate is mandatory for all international arrivals entering Entebbe International Airport. Routine travel immunizations including Hepatitis A, Tetanus, and Typhoid are recommended, along with physician-prescribed malaria prophylaxis such as Atovaquone-Proguanil or Doxycycline.

How does payment and permit security work?

Upon confirming your itinerary, a deposit covering the full statutory cost of your UWA gorilla and chimpanzee permits is required to lock in the official receipt and registration with the park authority. The remaining safari balance is settled 45 days prior to your arrival via bank wire transfer or secure online credit card portal.
